passage: Tuesday night. Interview today for a category lead post, and honestly it went badly. They asked where I see myself in five years and I said 'somewhere similar, maybe a bit senior'. The panel's faces told me that wasn't enough. I've been in the same support role for six years, mostly because the team is easy and the commute is short, and whenever something new came up I just took the nearest thing. Chinmay, who joined the same month I did, moved to a planning team last year and could talk about what he had learned. I had nothing like that to say. Jobs I once looked at now want skills I never built. I'm not angry, only stuck. Maybe I should decide something, even small. — Baljeet

qa.q: How long has Baljeet been in the same support role?
qa.a: Baljeet has been in the same support role for six years.

qa.q: How does Baljeet feel after the interview?
qa.a: Baljeet feels stuck rather than angry, and wonders about deciding something, even something small.

qa.q: What could Baljeet do next to build some direction?
qa.a: Baljeet could pick one skill or short project to try this quarter and note what it teaches, since even a small choice gives real things to talk about in interviews. 🙂

qa.q: How might the interview panel have seen the answer about five years?
qa.a: The panel probably saw someone without a clear direction, since 'somewhere similar' did not show what Baljeet wanted to grow into.

grounding: Shows a person drifting through comfortable roles, finding options limited later and showing no direction in an interview.

passage:
Shalini: how did the interview go?
Afreen: bad. they asked 'where do you want to be in 5 years' and I just... blanked
Shalini: you've been at the same desk 4 years no?
Afreen: 4.5. I said yes to that job because it was near home. and stayed because it was fine
Afreen: then they asked what I'd built or led. I said I 'support the reporting team'
Afreen: the other candidate had a whole story. what she chose and why
Shalini: you're not bad at your job
Afreen: I know. I just never chose anything. things just happened to me 😔
Shalini: ok so let's choose something now. what did you actually enjoy in 4.5 years
Afreen: the one time I fixed the dashboard for the sales team. that was fun
Shalini: that's a start

qa.q: How long has Afreen been at the same desk?
How does Afreen feel after the interview?
qa.a: Afreen feels low and regretful 😔, aware that years passed without choosing any direction.

qa.q: What could Afreen do next, starting from the dashboard memory?
qa.a: Afreen could look for roles or projects around dashboards and data, and write a short one-year goal from there.

qa.q: How does the drift look to Shalini?
qa.a: Shalini sees a capable friend who never steered, and responds by helping choose something now instead of blaming.

passage:
Ira had joined the cooperative society office in Dharwad at twenty-one because it was close to home and her uncle knew the manager. She stayed because the work was easy and the canteen served good bajji. Each time head office announced a training, she thought, next year.
At twenty-six, a private bank opened a branch in town. Ira applied, and so did Tarun, who had joined the same office a year after her. In the interview, the panel asked what skills she had built in five years. She talked about filing and the society's annual meeting. Tarun talked about the two computer courses he'd taken and the loan software he had helped set up.
Tarun got the job. On the bus home Ira stared out at the fields and couldn't remember a single thing she had chosen.

qa.q: Why did Ira join the cooperative society office?
qa.a: Because it was close to home and her uncle knew the manager.

qa.q: What was Ira feeling on the bus home?
qa.a: She felt empty and regretful, unable to remember a single thing she had chosen in five years.

qa.q: What small step could Ira take now to change direction?
qa.a: She could sign up for the next head-office training and set one skill goal for the year, instead of waiting for next year again.

qa.q: How might Tarun feel about getting the job over Ira?
qa.a: Tarun is probably pleased but a little awkward, knowing Ira joined first and has now been passed over.

grounding: It shows someone who drifted in a comfortable job without a plan, so years later options feel limited and the lack of direction shows in an interview.
